GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm.notes: braces <=3.0.3 stack-exhaustion denial of service on deeply nested brace patterns (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm). No fixed version is published, so no dependency range resolves around it: the only path in this repository is the dev-only release toolchain semantic-release -> @semantic-release/commit-analyzer -> micromatch -> braces. The advisory is a denial of service on brace expansion of attacker-supplied patterns; this project never expands untrusted glob input and devDependencies are not part of the published npm archive. Review before 2026-11-20: if braces ships a fix, or micromatch/semantic-release stops depending on it, delete this record; if the exception is still needed, re-justify it and move the date. Any other advisory fails the gate.

GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4.notes: glob >=9.0.0 <=14.0.1 AbortSignal cancellation bypass: after a timeout or abort, glob keeps traversing the filesystem instead of stopping (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4). Fixed upstream in glob@14.0.2. The only copy in this repository is the one bundled inside the npm CLI that the dev-only release toolchain installs: semantic-release -> @semantic-release/npm@13.2.0 -> npm@^11.6.2 (11.21.2) -> node_modules/npm/node_modules/glob@13.0.6. npm@11.21.2 (newest 11.x) and npm@12.2.2 (newest) both still bundle the vulnerable 13.0.6, @semantic-release/npm does not accept a glob range of its own, and npm ignores overrides for dependencies bundled inside its own tree, so no dependency range or lockfile change resolves it today. The finding is a denial of service on glob traversal of attacker-supplied patterns in the publishing toolchain; this project never expands untrusted glob input and devDependencies are not part of the published npm archive. Review before 2026-11-20: when an npm release that @semantic-release/npm accepts bundles glob >=14.0.2, run npm update npm, confirm the audit is clean, and delete this record; if the exception is still needed, re-justify it and move the date. Any other advisory fails the gate.

GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249.notes: minimatch >=7.0.0 <11.0.1 denial of service through globparts amplification, where one crafted pattern expands into work that exhausts time or memory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249). Fixed upstream in minimatch@11.0.1. The only vulnerable copy in this repository is the one bundled inside the npm CLI that the dev-only release toolchain installs: semantic-release -> @semantic-release/npm@13.2.0 -> npm@^11.6.2 (11.21.2) -> node_modules/npm/node_modules/minimatch@10.2.5. The top-level minimatch@11.0.3 used by the Pi peers is already fixed; npm@11.21.2 (newest 11.x) and npm@12.2.2 (newest) both still bundle the vulnerable 10.2.5, @semantic-release/npm does not accept a minimatch range of its own, and npm ignores overrides for dependencies bundled inside its own tree, so no dependency range or lockfile change resolves it today. The finding is a denial of service on pattern matching of attacker-supplied patterns in the publishing toolchain; this project never matches untrusted glob patterns and devDependencies are not part of the published npm archive. Review before 2026-11-20: when an npm release that @semantic-release/npm accepts bundles minimatch >=11.0.1, run npm update npm, confirm the audit is clean, and delete this record; if the exception is still needed, re-justify it and move the date. Any other advisory fails the gate.
